problem: Zero-shot VLM-based object navigation methods call large vision-language models at nearly every step, causing high compute cost and latency that hinder real-time deployment on physical robots.
motivation: Real robots need low-latency navigation, but strong zero-shot ObjectNav relies on frequent VLM queries. Much of the needed semantic knowledge (co-occurring objects, gateways, distractors) can be produced once per episode by a cheap text-only LLM, so the VLM only needs to be invoked at a few key decision moments.
key_idea: Generate a static knowledge base of Target-Context Cues once per episode with a text-only LLM, then use a call policy that invokes a multimodal VLM only for global route planning, deadlock resolution and final target verification, while a detector-driven VLM-free loop handles the rest.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations can be cited. The abstract implies that most steps do not need VLM reasoning when precomputed target-context cues and a real-time detector guide local navigation, and that selective VLM calls at critical moments preserve success while cutting cost.
method: Target-Context Cues: one text-only LLM call at the start of each episode produces likely support objects, strong co-occurring objects, Gateways and visually similar distractors, forming a static knowledge base
Call policy: selectively triggers the multimodal VLM only at a few key moments
Initial global route planning: the VLM is called at the start of navigation to plan a global route
Deadlock resolution: the VLM is called to break stalls such as visual loops
Final target verification: the VLM verifies final target candidates before stopping
VLM-free control loop: between VLM calls the agent uses a real-time object detector and local navigation guided by the precomputed cues

setting.backbone: Text-only LLM for cues + multimodal VLM for key calls (specific models not stated in the abstract) + real-time object detector
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (assumed; not stated in abstract)
setting.action_space: not stated in abstract (local navigation toward frontiers/detected targets)

numbers_note: abstract only; the abstract gives only relative reductions (about 48% fewer VLM calls, about 32% lower average episode time, comparable success), no absolute SR/SPL
results: On HM3D ObjectNav v2, VOCA reduces VLM calls by about 48% and average episode time by about 32% versus a strong baseline that calls models frequently, while keeping comparable success. The baseline is not named in the abstract.
limitations: Abstract-only reading: no absolute metrics, model names or ablations available
Relies on the quality of LLM-generated cues and on detector reliability; the call policy triggers are heuristic
Evaluated in simulation on HM3D; real-robot deployment is motivated but not shown in the abstract
compares_to: frequent-VLM-call zero-shot ObjectNav baseline (unnamed in abstract)
